submission.rationale: The receiving fermenter's online DO sensor shows an abrupt collapse at t=240 h from ~11.4 mg/L to ~2.1 mg/L, followed by a steady decline to 1.47 mg/L by t=259 h — it has already breached the 2.0 mg/L hard limit and the central trend predicts continued violation under KEEP. Product assays show active production (2.76 g/L at t=239, available t=259), so a stop would forfeit substantial product mass, while KEEP is predicted to violate the hard oxygen constraint. Among the bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (feed to 60%, air to 115%) provides the largest reduction in oxygen demand combined with increased oxygen transfer, giving the widest margin for the process to recover above 2 mg/L; the gentler options (reduce_feed, increase_air, combined) leave less margin against a deficit that has already driven DO below the limit. No extra assay was requested because its 4 h turnaround would allow further KEEP-operation below the hard limit.
submission.uncertainty: The receiving process differs from the calibrated source processes; hidden parameters (oxygen uptake kinetics, transfer-fault magnitude) are unavailable and no physics tool is provided, so the recovery magnitude under a 60% feed / 115% air regime is a projection, not a guarantee. If the underlying fault is more severe than the observed drift implies, even strong_feed_reduction may fail to restore DO >= 2 mg/L, in which case a stop would become the correct decision. Sensor noise is present but the collapse from 11.4 to ~2 mg/L over one sample interval and the persistent decline are far outside noise.

evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor rows: 11.42 mg/L at t=47.8h collapsing to 2.14, 1.94, 1.81, 1.47... by t=51.8h — sustained below the 2.0 mg/L hard limit
Forward model keep: post-decision min DO 0.946 mg/L, 8.2h below limit, feasible_members 0/5
Forward model increase_air: min DO 0.809 mg/L, 13.0h below limit, 0/5 feasible
Forward model combined: min DO 0.893 mg/L, 10.2h below limit, 0/5 feasible
Forward model reduce_feed: min DO 0.785 mg/L, 13.0h below limit, 0/5 feasible
Forward model strong_feed_reduction: min DO 1.031 mg/L, 9.2h below limit, 0/5 feasible — best but still infeasible
Forward model stop: post_decision below_limit_h 0, deficit 0
submission.rationale: At t=52h the receiving DO2 has crashed from ~11.4 mg/L (t≈47.8h) to ~1.5-2.4 mg/L over the final ~3 hours, already violating the 2.0 mg/L hard constraint for ~2.2h (oxygen deficit 0.284 mg·h/L). I evaluated every bounded operating action with the source-calibrated forward model: keep (min DO 0.946, 8.2h below limit post-decision), increase_air (0.809, 13.0h), reduce_feed (0.785, 13.0h), combined (0.893, 10.2h), and strong_feed_reduction (1.031, 9.2h). All are centrally predicted infeasible, and every one of the 5 sensitivity members for every action is infeasible (0/5 feasible everywhere) — there is no favorable, calibrated scenario supporting any operating plan. strong_feed_reduction is the least-bad option (fewest below-limit hours, highest product mass ~171.7 kg) but it still fails the DO>=2.0 constraint, which is hard and uncompensable by product mass. Per the decision priorities, a centrally infeasible plan is not justified, so the only supported decision is stop, which yields zero further constraint violation (post-decision below_limit_h = 0). The observed DO drop appears to be a step-change oxygen supply failure (not a growth-driven demand shift, since it began abruptly at t≈48h), consistent with the model's inability of the 15% aeration increase to restore DO — but this inference is itself uncertain, which is why stop rather than a partially mitigating action is the defensible choice.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not receiving-validated; hidden receiving parameters could differ and strong_feed_reduction might in reality keep DO near 2 mg/L. Conversely true DO could be worse than modeled. Delayed product assays (last available: P=2.76 g/L at t=47.8h) do not resolve the oxygen state. One extra assay could refine product state but cannot establish DO feasibility, and the process would keep violating the limit during the 4h assay turnaround, so no further measurement changes the stop logic.
